source_uses.fact: London LNRS is a strategic spatial nature-recovery tool with biodiversity priorities and a Local Habitat Map; it does not create new protections, designations or landowner obligations
Defra’s list was updated 26 June 2026 and records Greater London among published LNRS areas, following publication-status update on 11 March 2026
LNRS preparation is a statutory Environment Act 2021 requirement and strategies identify priorities, valuable areas and proposed recovery actions
London biodiversity policy uses LNRS to guide strategic nature recovery and connectivity
Draft London Plan 2026 GHR8 addresses Accessible Green Space and requires local plans to maintain designations and consider new population pressure
Draft PV6 Metropolitan Open Land policy retains a high-evidence exceptional-circumstances approach to release
Draft-plan glossary defines Accessible Green Space as freely accessible public green space and distinguishes access concepts
LBBD current page identifies 28 parks and green spaces in the borough
LBBD provides official local-open-space, country-park and recreation information
The Leys is an official borough open space combining formal sports pitches and natural country-park areas
Padnall Open Space is an official local lakeside green space and wildlife area
Draft-plan HRA recommended sufficient accessible-green-space provision to reduce recreation pressure on Epping Forest SAC; unresolved pathways remain explicit

examples: LNRS potential-measure mapping is strategic opportunity evidence and not a new statutory designation
The London LNRS map states some underlying information was correct as of August 2025, so finer current checks may be needed
A mapped LNRS opportunity does not by itself prevent or permit development
A borough park page proves an open-space asset exists but does not establish a candidate parcel boundary
Draft GHR8 Accessible Green Space is consultation policy and must not be treated as adopted
Draft MOL release criteria require evidence and cannot be converted into a simple development probability
HRA recreation-pressure findings are pathway evidence and not a blanket parcel exclusion
No promotion without exact parcel relation to current open-space/designation data plus applicable ecological assessment
